text.p: Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines earned $600 million revenues from passenger scheduled international flights during first 10 months of last year from $486 million in the same period of 1995, a company report obtained by Reuters said on Tuesday.
A large proportion of the revenues -- $157.5 million -- came from passengers flights between Russia and Western European destinations, the report said.
It said that South East Asian destinations earned $93.9 million, while $88.5 million came from flights to Eastern Europe.

The report said that North and South American flights earned $85.2 million, African and Middle Eastern flights - $64.5 million, and Commonwealth of Indepedent States and Baltic passenger operations - $11.4 million.
The report did not give any other financial results from last year, but the company has promised to reveal full results at the company shareholders' meeting scheduled for May 30.
